title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 9 — Biology | Immune System Diseases
description: Subject-wise test on Immune System Diseases (Biology) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 9. 25Q.
subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: The body's ability to resist the invasion of disease-causing microorganisms and their harmful effects is known as:

options.explanation: Infection refers to the invasion of a host organism's body tissues by disease-causing agents.
Pathogenesis refers to the development of a disease.
Immunity is the natural or acquired resistance of an organism to infection or disease.
Virulence refers to the degree of pathogenicity within a group or species of parasites as indicated by case fatality rates and/or the ability of the parasite to invade the tissues of the host.

questions.explanation: Immunity is the natural or acquired resistance of an organism to infection or disease.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: Which of the following diseases primarily targets and weakens the human immune system, making the body highly vulnerable to various opportunistic infections?

options.explanation: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs.
Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that is transmitted by the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito.
AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by the HIV virus, which attacks and destroys T-helper lymphocytes, crucial cells of the immune system, leading to immunodeficiency.
Cholera is a bacterial infection that causes severe diarrhea.

questions.explanation: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by the HIV virus, which attacks and destroys T-helper lymphocytes, crucial cells of the immune system, leading to immunodeficiency.

questions.question: Malaria is a well-known vector-borne disease. Which organism acts as the biological vector for transmitting the malarial parasite to humans?

options.explanation: Houseflies are not vectors of malaria.
Aedes mosquitoes are vectors of diseases such as dengue fever and Zika virus.
The female Anopheles mosquito transmits the Plasmodium parasite, which causes malaria, from an infected person to a healthy one.
Cockroaches are not vectors of malaria.

questions.explanation: The female Anopheles mosquito transmits the Plasmodium parasite, which causes malaria, from an infected person to a healthy one.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: Vaccines are a crucial tool for preventing infectious diseases. What do most vaccines typically contain to stimulate an immune response?

options.explanation: Vaccines do not contain strong, active, disease-causing pathogens.

options.text: Weakened or dead pathogens, or their parts
options.explanation: Vaccines work by introducing a weakened, inactivated, or partial form of a pathogen (antigen) into the body, which stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells without causing the actual disease.
Vaccines do not contain ready-made antibodies against the disease.
Vaccines do not contain antibiotics.

questions.explanation: Vaccines work by introducing a weakened, inactivated, or partial form of a pathogen (antigen) into the body, which stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells without causing the actual disease.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: A child receives a vaccination against Measles. The type of immunity developed in the child's body as a result of this vaccination is classified as:

options.explanation: Natural passive immunity is acquired through the transfer of antibodies from mother to child during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Artificial passive immunity is acquired through the administration of antibodies, such as immunoglobulins.
Natural active immunity is acquired through infection with a disease-causing agent, resulting in the production of antibodies and memory cells.
Vaccination involves the artificial introduction of antigens to stimulate the body's own immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells, thus developing active immunity artificially.

questions.explanation: Vaccination involves the artificial introduction of antigens to stimulate the body's own immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells, thus developing active immunity artificially.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: To effectively prevent the spread of diseases like cholera and typhoid, which are primarily water-borne infections, the most critical public health measure among the following is:

options.text: Regular physical exercise and a balanced diet
options.explanation: While regular physical exercise and a balanced diet are important for overall health, they are not the most critical measures for preventing the spread of water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid.

options.text: Mass vaccination drives against seasonal influenza
options.explanation: Vaccination against seasonal influenza is not directly relevant to preventing the spread of water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid.

options.text: Ensuring access to safe drinking water and proper sanitation facilities
options.explanation: Cholera and typhoid are spread through contaminated water and food. Therefore, ensuring safe drinking water and proper sanitation (hygienic disposal of waste) is the most effective preventive measure.

options.text: Promoting the use of insect repellents and mosquito nets
options.explanation: Insect repellents and mosquito nets are more relevant to preventing diseases spread by mosquitoes, such as malaria and dengue fever.

questions.explanation: Cholera and typhoid are spread through contaminated water and food. Therefore, ensuring safe drinking water and proper sanitation (hygienic disposal of waste) is the most effective preventive measure.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions describes a disorder where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and damages its own healthy cells and tissues, treating them as foreign invaders?

options.explanation: An allergic reaction is an overreaction of the immune system to a harmless antigen, resulting in inflammation and tissue damage.
An immunodeficiency disorder is a condition in which the immune system is impaired, making it difficult for the body to fight off infections.
In autoimmune diseases, the immune system fails to distinguish between self and non-self antigens, leading to an attack on the body's own tissues.
A hypersensitivity reaction is an overreaction of the immune system to an antigen, resulting in inflammation and tissue damage.

questions.explanation: In autoimmune diseases, the immune system fails to distinguish between self and non-self antigens, leading to an attack on the body's own tissues.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: A person suffering from persistent fever, cough, night sweats, and significant weight loss is diagnosed with Tuberculosis (TB). Based on its nature, Tuberculosis is an example of a:

options.explanation: Non-communicable diseases are not spread from person to person, such as heart disease or diabetes.
Genetic disorders are caused by genetic mutations or inherited traits, such as sickle cell anemia or cystic fibrosis.
Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and can spread from person to person, making it an infectious or communicable disease.
Deficiency diseases are caused by a lack of essential nutrients, such as scurvy or rickets.

questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and can spread from person to person, making it an infectious or communicable disease.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Vaccination provides long-term protection against specific infectious diseases. **Reason (R):** Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce memory cells, which can quickly mount a strong immune response upon subsequent exposure to the pathogen.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true as vaccines induce immunity. The reason correctly explains how this long-term protection is achieved – by the formation of memory cells that enable a rapid and robust secondary immune response.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason provided is the correct explanation for how vaccination provides long-term protection.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true as vaccines induce immunity. The reason correctly explains how this long-term protection is achieved – by the formation of memory cells that enable a rapid and robust secondary immune response.

questions.question: During a severe flood, a village experiences an outbreak of a disease characterized by high fever, severe muscle and joint pain, and a skin rash, later identified as Dengue fever. Given the typical mode of transmission for Dengue, what is the most immediate and effective measure the villagers should take to control the spread of this disease?

options.text: Organize a mass vaccination campaign for the entire village population.
options.explanation: While vaccination is an effective way to prevent many diseases, there is no widely available vaccine for Dengue fever.

options.text: Ensure all villagers wear face masks and maintain strict social distancing.
options.explanation: Face masks and social distancing are more relevant to preventing the spread of respiratory diseases, not vector-borne diseases like Dengue fever.

options.text: Eliminate all stagnant water sources around homes and in public areas.
options.explanation: Dengue fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water. Eliminating these breeding sites is the most effective immediate measure to control the mosquito population and thus prevent further spread of the disease.

options.text: Distribute broad-spectrum antibiotics to all affected individuals immediately.
options.explanation: Antibiotics are ineffective against viral infections like Dengue fever.

questions.explanation: Dengue fever is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water. Eliminating these breeding sites is the most effective immediate measure to control the mosquito population and thus prevent further spread of the disease.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the human immune system?

options.explanation: The regulation of blood sugar levels is primarily the function of the endocrine system, specifically the pancreas.

options.text: To protect the body from disease-causing pathogens
options.explanation: The immune system's main role is to defend the body against foreign invaders like bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other pathogens that can cause diseases.

options.text: To pump blood throughout the body
options.explanation: The pumping of blood throughout the body is the function of the heart, which is part of the circulatory system.

options.text: To break down food for energy
options.explanation: The breakdown of food for energy is primarily the function of the digestive system.

questions.explanation: The immune system's main role is to defend the body against foreign invaders like bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other pathogens that can cause diseases.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an autoimmune disease, where the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own healthy cells?

options.explanation: AIDS is an immunodeficiency disease caused by the HIV virus, not an autoimmune disease.
Malaria is an infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, not an autoimmune disease.
In autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, the immune system fails to distinguish between 'self' and 'non-self' antigens, leading it to attack the body's own healthy tissues.
Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, not an autoimmune disease.

questions.explanation: In autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, the immune system fails to distinguish between 'self' and 'non-self' antigens, leading it to attack the body's own healthy tissues.
questions.subject: maha9-biology

questions.question: Vaccination helps in preventing infectious diseases by stimulating the body to produce:

options.explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers produced by glands in the endocrine system and are not directly related to the immune response to vaccination.
Enzymes are biological catalysts involved in various metabolic processes but are not the primary products of the immune system in response to vaccination.
Vaccines stimulate the body to produce antibodies, which are proteins that recognize and bind to specific pathogens, helping to neutralize or remove them from the body.
Red blood cells are involved in transporting oxygen throughout the body and are not directly related to the immune response to vaccination.

questions.explanation: Vaccines introduce weakened or inactivated pathogens or their components (antigens) into the body, prompting the immune system to produce specific antibodies and memory cells, thus building active immunity without causing the actual disease.

questions.question: Which type of white blood cell is primarily targeted and destroyed by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?

options.explanation: Neutrophils are a type of white blood cell important in the innate immune response, especially against bacterial infections, but they are not the primary target of HIV.
HIV specifically attacks and destroys Helper T-cells, also known as CD4 cells, which are crucial for coordinating the entire immune response.
B-lymphocytes, or B cells, are important for the adaptive immune response, producing antibodies to fight pathogens, but they are not the primary target of HIV.
Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell involved in combating parasites and in allergic reactions, but they are not the primary target of HIV.

questions.explanation: HIV specifically attacks and destroys Helper T-cells, also known as CD4 cells. These cells are crucial for coordinating the entire immune response, and their destruction leads to a severely compromised immune system.

questions.question: A child receives a vaccine against measles. This type of immunity, where the body actively produces its own antibodies and memory cells in response to an antigen, is known as:

options.explanation: Passive immunity involves the transfer of antibodies from one person to another, providing temporary protection, and is not the result of the body producing its own antibodies in response to an antigen.
Innate immunity is the body's first line of defense, providing non-specific protection against pathogens, and is not the result of the body producing antibodies in response to an antigen.
Active acquired immunity is developed when the immune system produces its own antibodies and memory cells in response to an antigen, either through natural infection or via vaccination.

Naturally acquired passive immunity refers to the transfer of antibodies from mother to child during pregnancy or breastfeeding, providing temporary protection, and is not the result of the body producing its own antibodies in response to an antigen.

questions.explanation: Active acquired immunity is developed when the immune system produces its own antibodies and memory cells in response to an antigen, either through natural infection or via vaccination.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Antibiotics are effective against bacterial infections but generally not against viral infections. Reason (R): Antibiotics specifically target bacterial cell wall synthesis, protein synthesis, or DNA replication, mechanisms that are absent in viruses.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Antibiotics are effective against bacterial infections because they target specific processes in bacteria, such as cell wall synthesis, protein synthesis, or DNA replication, which are not present in viruses, making them ineffective against viral infections.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because R provides a correct explanation for why antibiotics are effective against bacterial infections but not against viral infections.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because R is true; antibiotics do specifically target bacterial cell wall synthesis, protein synthesis, or DNA replication, which are mechanisms absent in viruses.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because A is true; antibiotics are generally effective against bacterial infections but not against viral infections.

questions.explanation: Antibiotics are designed to interfere with specific metabolic processes or structures unique to bacteria. Viruses are intracellular parasites that use host cell machinery and lack these bacterial targets, making antibiotics ineffective against them.

questions.question: A person suffering from a severe allergic reaction experiences symptoms like rapid swelling of the face and throat, difficulty breathing, and a sudden drop in blood pressure. This life-threatening systemic allergic reaction is called:

options.explanation: Autoimmunity refers to the immune system's attack on the body's own cells, tissues, and organs, which is different from an allergic reaction.
Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that can affect multiple body systems simultaneously.
Immunodeficiency refers to a state in which the immune system's ability to fight infectious disease is either impaired or absent, which is different from an allergic reaction.
Hypersensitivity is a broader term for an exaggerated immune response, of which anaphylaxis is a severe form, but it is not the specific term for this life-threatening systemic allergic reaction.

questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that can affect multiple body systems simultaneously, leading to symptoms like airway constriction, swelling, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between innate and acquired (adaptive) immunity?

options.text: Innate immunity is specific to particular pathogens, while acquired immunity is non-specific.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because it reverses the characteristics of innate and acquired immunity.

options.text: Innate immunity involves the formation of memory cells, while acquired immunity does not.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because it is actually acquired immunity that involves the formation of memory cells, not innate immunity.

options.text: Innate immunity is present from birth and provides general, non-specific protection, while acquired immunity develops after exposure to pathogens and is specific with memory.
options.explanation: This statement correctly differentiates between innate and acquired immunity, highlighting their distinct characteristics.

options.text: Innate immunity is slower to respond to pathogens, while acquired immunity provides an immediate response.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because it is actually innate immunity that provides an immediate response to pathogens, while acquired immunity takes time to develop.

questions.explanation: Innate immunity is the body's first line of non-specific defense, present at birth, offering immediate, general protection. Acquired (or adaptive) immunity is highly specific, develops over time after exposure to pathogens, and involves memory cells for a faster and stronger response upon re-exposure.

questions.question: A 35-year-old patient frequently suffers from severe and recurring infections such as pneumonia, candidiasis (fungal infection), and Kaposi's sarcoma (a type of cancer). Blood tests consistently reveal a significantly reduced count of CD4 T-lymphocytes. Based on this information, which of the following conditions is most likely affecting the patient?

options.explanation: Malaria is an infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and is not directly related to a reduced count of CD4 T-lymphocytes.

Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and, while it can be opportunistic in immunocompromised individuals, the combination of symptoms and low CD4 count points more directly to AIDS.
The recurring opportunistic infections and a drastically lowered CD4 T-cell count are classic indicators of Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS).
Hepatitis B is a viral infection that affects the liver and is not directly related to the symptoms and low CD4 count described.

questions.explanation: The recurring opportunistic infections and a drastically lowered CD4 T-cell count are classic indicators of Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), which is the final stage of HIV infection where the immune system is severely compromised.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why individuals with a compromised immune system (e.g., due to HIV infection or immunosuppressant drugs) are highly susceptible to developing multiple types of infections, including those from normally harmless microbes?

options.text: Their body produces an excess of antibodies, which then attack healthy cells.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because an excess of antibodies attacking healthy cells describes an autoimmune response, not the reason for susceptibility to infections in individuals with a compromised immune system.

options.text: Their digestive system is unable to absorb essential nutrients, leading to general weakness.
options.explanation: While malabsorption can lead to weakness and potentially increase susceptibility to infections, it does not directly explain why individuals with a compromised immune system are susceptible to a wide range of infections.

options.text: Their immune cells overreact to minor threats, exhausting the immune response prematurely.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because it describes an overactive immune response, which is different from the compromised immune system's inability to effectively respond to pathogens.

options.text: The reduction in functional immune cells (like Helper T-cells) impairs the body's ability to recognize, coordinate, and fight off diverse pathogens effectively.
options.explanation: This option correctly explains that the reduction in functional immune cells, such as Helper T-cells, is the reason individuals with a compromised immune system are highly susceptible to developing multiple types of infections.

questions.explanation: A compromised immune system means that the key cells responsible for identifying and eliminating pathogens, particularly Helper T-cells, are either reduced in number or dysfunctional. This loss of immune coordination leaves the body vulnerable to a wide range of infections, including those from opportunistic microbes that a healthy immune system would easily control.

questions.question: Which virus is primarily responsible for causing Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS)?

options.explanation: HPV is responsible for causing cervical cancer and other diseases, but not AIDS.
HIV is the primary cause of AIDS.
HBV is responsible for causing hepatitis B, but not AIDS.
HSV is responsible for causing herpes, but not AIDS.

questions.explanation: AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which attacks the immune system.

questions.question: An exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment, such as pollen or dust mites, is commonly known as:

options.explanation: Autoimmunity involves the immune system attacking the body's own cells.
Immunodeficiency is a weakened immune system.
An allergy is an overreaction of the immune system to harmless substances.
Immunization is the process of becoming immune to a disease.

questions.explanation: An allergy is an overreaction of the immune system to harmless substances (allergens) in the environment.

questions.question: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) primarily weakens the immune system by specifically targeting and destroying which type of cells?

options.explanation: Red blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen, but are not targeted by HIV.
B-lymphocytes are involved in antibody production, but are not the primary target of HIV.
Helper T-lymphocytes are crucial for coordinating the immune response and are the primary target of HIV.
Neutrophils are a type of white blood cell, but are not the primary target of HIV.

questions.explanation: HIV specifically targets and destroys helper T-lymphocytes (also known as CD4 cells), which are crucial for coordinating the immune response.

questions.question: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is a combination of medicines used to treat HIV infection. The primary goal of ART is to:

options.text: Completely eradicate the HIV virus from the body.
options.explanation: ART does not completely eradicate the virus, but reduces the viral load.

options.text: Stimulate the production of new B-lymphocytes.
options.explanation: ART does not directly stimulate the production of new B-lymphocytes.

options.text: Reduce the viral load and preserve immune function.
options.explanation: The primary goal of ART is to reduce the viral load and preserve immune function.

options.text: Prevent the transmission of other sexually transmitted infections.
options.explanation: While ART can reduce the risk of transmission, it is not the primary goal.

questions.explanation: The primary goal of ART is to reduce the viral load and preserve immune function.
